heath_proof: For from the rational area BC let the medial area BD be subtracted; I say that the “side” of the remainder EC becomes one of two irrational straight lines, either an apotome or a minor straight line. For let a rational straight line FG be set out, to FG let there be applied the rectangular parallelogram GH equal to BC, and let GK equal to DB be subtracted; therefore the remainder EC is equal to LH. Since then BC is rational, and BD medial, while BC is equal to GH, and BD to GK, therefore GH is rational, and GK medial. And they are applied to the rational straight line FG; therefore FH is rational and commensurable in length with FG, [X. 20] while FK is rational and incommensurable in length with FG; [X. 22] therefore FH is incommensurable in length with FK. [X. 13] Therefore FH, FK are rational straight lines commensurable in square only; therefore KH is an apotome [X. 73], and KF the annex to it. Now the square on HF is greater than the square on FK by the square on a straight line either commensurable with HF or not commensurable. First, let the square on it be greater by the square on a straight line commensurable with it. Now the whole HF is commensurable in length with the rational straight line FG set out; therefore KH is a first apotome. [X. Deff. III. 1] But the “side” of the rectangle contained by a rational straight line and a first apotome is an apotome. [X. 91] Therefore the “side” of LH, that is, of EC, is an apotome. But, if the square on HF is greater than the square on FK by the square on a straight line incommensurable with HF, while the whole FH is commensurable in length with the rational straight line FG set out, KH is a fourth apotome. [X. Deff. III. 4] But the “side” of the rectangle contained by a rational straight line and a fourth apotome is minor. [X. 94]

10.108
**Statement:** If from a rational area a medial area be subtracted, the âsideâ of the remaining area becomes one of two irrational straight lines, either an apotome or a minor straight line.

**Step 1.** Let the rational area be AB, let the medial area CD be subtracted from it, and let the remainder be EF, so that EF = AB - CD. We must show that the "side" of EF (the straight line whose square equals EF) is either an apotome or a minor straight line.

**Step 2.** Let a rational straight line r be set out. Apply the rational area AB to r, producing as breadth the straight line g, so that AB = r * g. Since AB is a rational area and r is a rational straight line, by 10.20, g is rational and commensurable in length with r.

**Step 3.** Apply the medial area CD to r, producing as breadth the straight line h, so that CD = r * h. Now CD is medial, meaning it is irrational but commensurable with the square on some medial straight line m (by D10.1.4). By 10.22, the square on m applied to the rational straight line r produces a breadth that is rational and incommensurable in length with r. Since CD is commensurable with the square on m, and both CD and the square on m are applied to the same rational line r, the breadths are proportional to the areas. By 10.11, since the areas are commensurable, the breadths are commensurable. Therefore h is commensurable in length with a straight line that is rational and incommensurable in length with r. By 10.12, h is rational. By 10.13, since h is commensurable with a line incommensurable in length with r, h is also incommensurable in length with r.

**Step 4.** Since g is rational and commensurable in length with r, and h is rational and commensurable in length with r only in square (being incommensurable in length with r), both g and h are commensurable in square with r. By 10.12, g and h are commensurable in square with each other. However, since g is commensurable in length with r while h is incommensurable in length with r, by 10.13, g and h are incommensurable in length with each other. Therefore g and h are rational straight lines commensurable in square only.

**Step 5.** Since AB is greater than CD (a rational area exceeds a medial area, for if they were equal a rational area would equal a medial area, which is impossible since a rational area is commensurable with the square on the rational line while a medial area is not, by D10.1.4), and AB = r * g while CD = r * h, it follows that g is greater than h. By 10.73, since g and h are rational straight lines commensurable in square only and g > h, the straight line g - h is an apotome with g as the whole and h as the annex.

**Step 6.** Now EF = AB - CD = r * g - r * h = r * (g - h). So EF is the rectangle contained by the rational straight line r and the apotome g - h. The "side" of EF is determined by the order of the apotome g - h.

**Step 7.** Since g is commensurable in length with the rational straight line r, exactly one of two cases holds for the apotome g - h, depending on whether the square on g exceeds the square on h by the square on a straight line commensurable or incommensurable in length with g.

**Step 8.** Case 1: Suppose the square on g is greater than the square on h by the square on a straight line commensurable in length with g. Since g (the whole of the apotome) is commensurable in length with the rational straight line r, by D10.3.1, g - h is a first apotome. By 10.91, since EF is contained by the rational straight line r and a first apotome, the "side" of EF is an apotome.

**Step 9.** Case 2: Suppose the square on g is greater than the square on h by the square on a straight line incommensurable in length with g. Since g (the whole of the apotome) is commensurable in length with the rational straight line r, by D10.3.4, g - h is a fourth apotome. By 10.94, since EF is contained by the rational straight line r and a fourth apotome, the "side" of EF is a minor straight line.

**Step 10.** Therefore, in either case, the "side" of the remaining area EF is either an apotome or a minor straight line. Q.E.D.
